  <bpmn:process id="Process_Applicant" name="Job applicant" isExecutable="false">

    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_NoOffer" name="Application closed without offer"/>

    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="Catch_ApplicantRating" name="Applicant rating received">

      </bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
    </bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>
    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_PublishReviews" name="Make company reviews visible to applicants"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_ReviewPublished" name="Reviews published"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="SF_C1" sourceRef="StartEvent_Company" targetRef="SendTask_ConfirmReceipt"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="SF_C2" sourceRef="SendTask_ConfirmReceipt" targetRef="Task_RateApplication"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="SF_C3" sourceRef="Task_RateApplication" targetRef="Gateway_InterviewWanted"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="SF_C4" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_InterviewWanted" targetRef="SendTask_ProposeInterview"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="SF_C5" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_InterviewWanted" targetRef="Merge_Interview"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="SF_C6" sourceRef="SendTask_ProposeInterview" targetRef="Merge_Interview"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="SF_C7" sourceRef="Merge_Interview" targetRef="Gateway_WantsToHire"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="SF_C8" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_WantsToHire" targetRef="SendTask_WorkOffer"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="SF_C9" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_WantsToHire" targetRef="End_NoOffer"/>

rules.instruction: When the description states that a participant performs a stated action (for example sending an item, confirming receipt of an item, or assessing an item) and that action is placed in the order before a later decision or step, while another party's response or a later arrival is described only as a result of that action: Model each such stated action as its own user task in the lane of the participant who performs it, at the point the description orders it. Do not replace the action with a start event that represents the arrival of its result, and do not let a gateway that only tests a condition, or a separate task created for a repeated check, stand in for the action itself. Connect the action's outgoing flow to the next element the description ties to it.
rules.situation: the description states that a participant performs a stated action (for example sending an item, confirming receipt of an item, or assessing an item) and that action is placed in the order before a later decision or step, while another party's response or a later arrival is described only as a result of that action

rules.instruction: When the description states a yes/no condition that decides which branch follows a step, and the same condition is stated in the sentence that introduces that decision: Label the exclusive gateway as a yes/no question that repeats the condition in the description's own wording, and place it at the point where the description ties that condition to the step. Do not reuse a condition from a neighboring sentence or a condition about another action. Give the task that the condition controls the action verb and object the description uses, and do not add a separate reporting-style gateway or task that the description does not state.
rules.situation: the description states a yes/no condition that decides which branch follows a step, and the same condition is stated in the sentence that introduces that decision

rules.instruction: When the description states that a receiving party must confirm receipt of an item that another party submitted to it and must also evaluate that item, as mandatory actions of the receiving party: Model the receiving party's confirmation and evaluation as separate user tasks in that party's lane, placed after the submitting task and before any decision that depends on the evaluation. Do not model the receipt as a new start event, and do not replace the evaluation with a gateway or a flow that has no task.
rules.situation: the description states that a receiving party must confirm receipt of an item that another party submitted to it and must also evaluate that item, as mandatory actions of the receiving party

rules.instruction: When the description states a recurring obligation that a participant must fulfil at a stated point in the process, and a later stated condition decides whether that obligation still applies and the participant keeps fulfilling it: Model the recurring fulfilment as a user task in the lane of the participant who performs it, placed in the sequence where the description orders it. Follow it with a yes/no exclusive gateway whose label repeats the stopping condition in the description's wording. Route one branch back to the fulfilment task while the obligation continues, and route the other branch on to the next step the description ties to the end of the obligation. Do not place the fulfilment task before or outside the step the description orders it after, and do not replace the recurring task with a gateway alone.
rules.situation: the description states a recurring obligation that a participant must fulfil at a stated point in the process, and a later stated condition decides whether that obligation still applies and the participant keeps fulfilling it
